- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.5) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overshoot; cap forecast peaks at 1.2x the 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment is negative and prices are trending downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a 3–5% downward bias to forecast if recent 7-day average is below 70.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from 14-day avg), model overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; apply a 2–4 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 10–15% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating +/–0.3), model exhibits high variance; use a 30-day rolling median as a baseline and adjust forecast by ±2% based on sentiment directionality.
